ACADEMIC TEAM PROJECT · ERGONOMICS

Ergonomic Pipetting Concept

A foot-pedal pipetting concept co-developed with user and occupational-therapy input to explore a different interaction for repetitive laboratory work.

Context

Academic team project at Johnson & Wales University.

My contribution

Co-development of the concept and prototypes as part of the student team.

Recognition

Second place in JWU Sharkfest, 2022.

DESIGN DIRECTION

Move an input away from the hand.

The team explored alternative ways to operate a pipette, including a foot-pedal concept. User and occupational-therapy input informed the project. The work is presented as an ergonomic design exploration—not as a clinically validated device, certified medical product, or proof of injury prevention.

PROTOTYPES

Foot pedal

The concept selected for further exploration within the academic project.

Pistol grip

An alternative interaction concept considered by the team.

Palm grip

Another physical concept used to compare possible ways of changing the hand interaction.

WHAT THE PROJECT DEMONSTRATES

User input, physical concepts, and iteration.

This project shows how I approach a practical human problem through collaboration and physical prototyping while keeping the claims proportional to the evidence.
